sanskrit: vyāpakaṃ sarvabhūteṣu vartate 'pratighaṃ manaḥ manasy antarhitaṃ dvāraṃ deham āsthāya mānasam
english: All-pervading, unobstructed, the mind moves within every being; hidden within the mind is its doorway, the mental seat that abides within the body.

sanskrit: yat tat sadasad avyaktaṃ svapity asmin nidarśanam sarvabhūtātmabhūtasthaṃ tad adhyātmaguṇaṃ viduḥ
english: That unmanifest which is both being and non-being sleeps within this body—the proof of it lies here; abiding as the inner self of all creatures, the wise know it as the quality of the supreme Self.

sanskrit: lipseta manasā yaś ca saṃkalpād aiśvaraṃ guṇam ātmaprabhāvāt taṃ vidyāt sarvā hy ātmani devatāḥ
english: Whoever would attain by mind, through resolve, the lordly power, let him know it springs from the Self's own might—for all the deities dwell within the Self.

sanskrit: evaṃ hi tapasā yuktam arkavat tamasaḥ param trailokyaprakṛtir dehī tapasā taṃ maheśvaram
english: Thus the embodied one, joined to austerity, shines beyond darkness like the sun; the very source of the three worlds, through austerity he becomes that Great Lord.

sanskrit: tapo hy adhiṣṭhitaṃ devais tapoghnam asurais tamaḥ etad devāsurair guptaṃ tad āhur jñānalakṣaṇam
english: Austerity is upheld by the gods, while darkness, the slayer of austerity, is upheld by the asuras; this contest, guarded by gods and demons alike, they call the mark of true knowledge.

sanskrit: sattvaṃ rajas tamaś ceti devāsuraguṇān viduḥ sattvaṃ devaguṇaṃ vidyād itarāv āsurau guṇau
english: Goodness, passion, and darkness—these they know as the qualities of gods and demons; let one know goodness (sattva) as the divine quality, and the other two as the demonic ones.

sanskrit: brahma tat paramaṃ vedyam amṛtaṃ jyotir akṣaram ye vidur bhāvitātmānas te yānti paramāṃ gatim
english: That supreme Brahman is to be known—the deathless light, the imperishable; those of perfected self who know it attain the highest goal.

sanskrit: hetumac chakyam ākhyātum etāvaj jñānacakṣuṣā pratyāhāreṇa vā śakyam avyaktaṃ brahma veditum
english: Only this much, grounded in reason, can be set forth by the eye of knowledge; yet through the withdrawal of the senses the unmanifest Brahman too can be known.

sanskrit: gurur uvāca na sa veda paraṃ dharmaṃ yo na veda catuṣṭayam vyaktāvyakte ca yat tattvaṃ saṃprāptaṃ paramarṣiṇā
english: The teacher said: He does not know the supreme law who does not know the fourfold scheme, and that truth concerning the manifest and the unmanifest which was attained by the supreme seer.

sanskrit: vyaktaṃ mṛtyumukhaṃ vidyād avyaktam amṛtaṃ padam pravṛttilakṣaṇaṃ dharmam ṛṣir nārāyaṇo 'bravīt
english: Let one know the manifest as the mouth of death, and the unmanifest as the deathless state; the seer Nārāyaṇa proclaimed the law marked by engagement in action.

sanskrit: atraivāvasthitaṃ sarvaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram nivṛttilakṣaṇaṃ dharmam avyaktaṃ brahma śāśvatam
english: Within this very realm rests the whole triple world, with all that moves and is still; the law marked by withdrawal is the unmanifest, the eternal Brahman.

sanskrit: pravṛttilakṣaṇaṃ dharmaṃ prajāpatir athābravīt pravṛttiḥ punarāvṛttir nivṛttiḥ paramā gatiḥ
english: The law marked by engagement Prajāpati then declared: engagement is rebirth again and again, while withdrawal is the supreme goal.

sanskrit: tāṃ gatiṃ paramām eti nivṛttiparamo muniḥ jñānatattvaparo nityaṃ śubhāśubhanidarśakaḥ
english: That supreme goal the sage attains who is devoted above all to withdrawal, ever intent on the truth of knowledge, discerning the good and the evil.

sanskrit: tad evam etau vijñeyāv avyaktapuruṣāv ubhau avyaktapuruṣābhyāṃ tu yat syād anyan mahattaram
english: Thus these two are to be understood—the Unmanifest and the Spirit, both; yet whatever may be greater than the Unmanifest and the Spirit—

sanskrit: taṃ viśeṣam avekṣeta viśeṣeṇa vicakṣaṇaḥ anādyantāv ubhāv etāv aliṅgau cāpy ubhāv api
english: that distinction let the discerning one observe with discernment; both of these are without beginning or end, and both alike are without mark.

sanskrit: ubhau nityau sūkṣmatarau mahadbhyaś ca mahattarau sāmānyam etad ubhayor evaṃ hy anyad viśeṣaṇam
english: Both are eternal, subtler than the subtle, and greater than the great; this is what they hold in common—and thus is their difference also.

sanskrit: prakṛtyā sargadharmiṇyā tathā trividhasattvayā viparītam ato vidyāt kṣetrajñasya ca lakṣaṇam
english: Primordial Nature has the property of creation and is of threefold disposition; opposite to this, let one know, is the mark of the Knower of the field.

sanskrit: prakṛteś ca vikārāṇāṃ draṣṭāram aguṇānvitam agrāhyau puruṣāv etāv aliṅgatvād asaṃhitau
english: He is the witness of Nature and her transformations, untouched by the qualities; these two—Spirit and Nature—are imperceptible, and being without mark, they remain unconjoined.

sanskrit: saṃyogalakṣaṇotpattiḥ karmajā gṛhyate yayā karaṇaiḥ karmanirvṛttaiḥ kartā yad yad viceṣṭate kīrtyate śabdasaṃjñābhiḥ ko 'ham eṣo 'py asāv iti
english: Their union has the mark of an origination born of action, grasped through the instruments brought into being by action; whatever the agent does through these, it is named by words and conceptions—'Who am I? This one too, that one—'

sanskrit: uṣṇīṣavān yathā vastrais tribhir bhavati saṃvṛtaḥ saṃvṛto 'yaṃ tathā dehī sattvarājasatāmasaiḥ
english: As a man wearing a turban is wrapped in three garments, so this embodied one is enveloped by the qualities of goodness, passion, and darkness.

sanskrit: tasmāc catuṣṭayaṃ vedyam etair hetubhir ācitam yathāsaṃjño hy ayaṃ samyag antakāle na muhyati
english: Therefore the fourfold scheme is to be known, heaped together by these causes; for he who rightly understands its conception is not bewildered at the hour of death.

sanskrit: śriyaṃ divyām abhiprepsur brahma vāṅmanasā śuciḥ śārīrair niyamair ugraiś caren niṣkalmaṣaṃ tapaḥ
english: He who longs for the divine splendor of Brahman, pure in speech and mind, should practice spotless austerity through fierce bodily disciplines.

sanskrit: trailokyaṃ tapasā vyāptam antarbhūtena bhāsvatā sūryaś ca candramāś caiva bhāsatas tapasā divi
english: The three worlds are pervaded by austerity, the radiant power dwelling within; both the sun and the moon shine in the heavens by virtue of austerity.

sanskrit: pratāpas tapaso jñānaṃ loke saṃśabditaṃ tapaḥ rajastamoghnaṃ yat karma tapasas tat svalakṣaṇam
english: The glow of austerity is knowledge—austerity is renowned throughout the world; that action which destroys passion and darkness is the very mark of austerity.

sanskrit: brahmacaryam ahiṃsā ca śārīraṃ tapa ucyate vāṅmanoniyamaḥ sāmyaṃ mānasaṃ tapa ucyate
english: Chastity and non-injury are called bodily austerity; the restraint of speech and mind, and equanimity, are called mental austerity.

sanskrit: vidhijñebhyo dvijātibhyo grāhyam annaṃ viśiṣyate āhāraniyamenāsya pāpmā naśyati rājasaḥ
english: Food to be received from twice-born men who know the ordinances is held to be best; by restraint of his diet the evil born of passion is destroyed.

sanskrit: vaimanasyaṃ ca viṣaye yānty asya karaṇāni ca tasmāt tanmātram ādadyād yāvad atra prayojanam
english: His faculties grow averse to their objects; therefore let him take only so much as is needed for the purpose here.

sanskrit: antakāle vayotkarṣāc chanaiḥ kuryād anāturaḥ evaṃ yuktena manasā jñānaṃ tad upapadyate
english: At the close of life, with advancing age, let him do this gradually, untroubled; thus, with a mind so disciplined, that knowledge arises in him.

sanskrit: rajasā cāpy ayaṃ dehī dehavāñ śabdavac caret kāryair avyāhatamatir vairāgyāt prakṛtau sthitaḥ ā dehād apramādāc ca dehāntād vipramucyate
english: Even amid passion this embodied one, while he bears a body, should move as sound moves through it; his judgment unimpaired by his tasks, fixed in Nature through dispassion, by vigilance until the body's end he is wholly freed when the body ends.

sanskrit: hetuyuktaḥ sadotsargo bhūtānāṃ pralayas tathā parapratyayasarge tu niyataṃ nātivartate
english: Joined to its cause, the dissolution of beings is a constant letting-go; yet in a creation dependent on another's cognition, he assuredly does not transgress the appointed bound.

sanskrit: bhavāntaprabhavaprajñā āsate ye viparyayam dhṛtyā dehān dhārayanto buddhisaṃkṣiptamānasāḥ sthānebhyo dhvaṃsamānāś ca sūkṣmatvāt tān upāsate
english: Those whose wisdom reaches to the end and the origin of becoming dwell amid this confusion, sustaining their bodies by firmness, their minds drawn inward by intellect; though falling away from their stations, they revere those subtle truths by reason of their subtlety.

sanskrit: yathāgamaṃ ca tat sarvaṃ buddhyā tan naiva budhyate dehāntaṃ kaś cid anvāste bhāvitātmā nirāśrayaḥ yukto dhāraṇayā kaś cit sattāṃ ke cid upāsate
english: All this, though pursued according to scripture, is not truly grasped by the intellect; one of perfected self, dependent on nothing, attends upon the body's end; another, joined in concentration, and yet others revere pure Being.

sanskrit: abhyasyanti paraṃ devaṃ vidyutsaṃśabditākṣaram antakāle hy upāsannās tapasā dagdhakilbiṣāḥ
english: They practice meditation on the supreme God, the Imperishable proclaimed as lightning; drawing near him at the hour of death, their sins burnt away by austerity—

sanskrit: sarva ete mahātmāno gacchanti paramāṃ gatim sūkṣmaṃ viśeṣaṇaṃ teṣām avekṣec chāstracakṣuṣā
english: all these great souls go to the supreme goal; their subtle distinction one should observe with the eye of scripture.

sanskrit: dehaṃ tu paramaṃ vidyād vimuktam aparigraham antarikṣād anyataraṃ dhāraṇāsaktamānasam
english: Let one know the supreme body as liberated and free of possessions; the mind fastened upon concentration is set apart, as it were, from the very air.

sanskrit: martyalokād vimucyante vidyāsaṃyuktamānasāḥ brahmabhūtā virajasas tato yānti parāṃ gatim
english: Those whose minds are joined to knowledge are released from the world of mortals; become Brahman, freed of passion, they then go to the highest goal.

sanskrit: kaṣāyavarjitaṃ jñānaṃ yeṣām utpadyate 'calam te yānti paramāṃl lokān viśudhyanto yathābalam
english: Those in whom unshakable knowledge, void of every stain, arises go to the supreme worlds, growing purified each according to his strength.

sanskrit: bhagavantam ajaṃ divyaṃ viṣṇum avyaktasaṃjñitam bhāvena yānti śuddhā ye jñānatṛptā nirāśiṣaḥ
english: The pure ones, content in knowledge and free of all longing, attain through devotion the blessed Lord Viṣṇu—the unborn, the divine, called the Unmanifest.

sanskrit: jñātvātmasthaṃ hariṃ caiva nivartante na te 'vyayāḥ prāpya tat paramaṃ sthānaṃ modante 'kṣaram avyayam
english: Having known Hari dwelling within the Self, those imperishable ones return no more; reaching that supreme abode, they rejoice in the deathless, the unfailing.

sanskrit: etāvad etad vijñānam etad asti ca nāsti ca tṛṣṇābaddhaṃ jagat sarvaṃ cakravat parivartate
english: This is the whole of that knowledge: this both is and is not; the entire world, bound fast by craving, revolves like a wheel.

sanskrit: bisatantur yathaivāyam antaḥsthaḥ sarvato bise tṛṣṇātantur anādyantas tathā dehagataḥ sadā
english: Just as this fiber runs within the lotus-stalk, present throughout it on every side, so the thread of craving, without beginning or end, runs ever through the embodied being.

sanskrit: sūcyā sūtraṃ yathā vastre saṃsārayati vāyakaḥ tadvat saṃsārasūtraṃ hi tṛṣṇāsūcyā nibadhyate
english: As the weaver, with his needle, draws the thread through the cloth, so the thread of transmigration is stitched together by the needle of craving.

sanskrit: vikāraṃ prakṛtiṃ caiva puruṣaṃ ca sanātanam yo yathāvad vijānāti sa vitṛṣṇo vimucyate
english: He who rightly understands transformation, Nature, and the eternal Spirit becomes free of craving and is liberated.

sanskrit: prakāśaṃ bhagavān etad ṛṣir nārāyaṇo 'mṛtam bhūtānām anukampārthaṃ jagāda jagato hitam
english: This illumination, this deathless truth, the blessed seer Nārāyaṇa proclaimed out of compassion for living beings, for the welfare of the world.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kena vṛttena vṛttajño janako mithilādhipaḥ jagāma mokṣaṃ dharmajño bhogān utsṛjya mānuṣān
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: By what conduct did Janaka, the lord of Mithilā, learned in conduct and knowing the law, attain liberation, casting off the pleasures of mortals?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam yena vṛttena vṛttajñaḥ sa jagāma mahat sukham
english: Bhīṣma said: On this too they recount an ancient tale—the conduct by which that knower of conduct attained the great happiness.

sanskrit: janako janadevas tu mithilāyāṃ janādhipaḥ aurdhvadehikadharmāṇām āsīd yukto vicintane
english: Now Janaka, called Janadeva, the ruler of men in Mithilā, was engaged in reflecting upon the duties concerning the soul's life after death.

sanskrit: tasya sma śatam ācāryā vasanti satataṃ gṛhe darśayantaḥ pṛthag dharmān nānāpāṣaṇḍavādinaḥ
english: In his house a hundred teachers dwelt continually, setting forth diverse doctrines, the upholders of many heretical creeds.

sanskrit: sa teṣāṃ pretyabhāve ca pretyajātau viniścaye āgamasthaḥ sa bhūyiṣṭham ātmatattve na tuṣyati
english: Though firmly grounded in their scriptures regarding the state after death and the rebirth that follows, he found, for the most part, no satisfaction in the truth of the Self.

sanskrit: tatra pañcaśikho nāma kāpileyo mahāmuniḥ paridhāvan mahīṃ kṛtsnāṃ jagāma mithilām api
english: Now there was a great sage named Pañcaśikha, of Kapila's line, who, roaming the whole earth, came at last to Mithilā as well.

sanskrit: sarvasaṃnyāsadharmāṇāṃ tattvajñānaviniścaye suparyavasitārthaś ca nirdvaṃdvo naṣṭasaṃśayaḥ
english: In the determination of the true knowledge of all the laws of renunciation he had reached the perfect end of his purpose—beyond the pairs of opposites, his every doubt destroyed.

sanskrit: ṛṣīṇām āhur ekaṃ yaṃ kāmād avasitaṃ nṛṣu śāśvataṃ sukham atyantam anvicchan sa sudurlabham
english: Him they call the one among the seers who, of his own will, had settled among men; seeking the eternal, the utmost happiness, that one most hard to win.

sanskrit: yam āhuḥ kapilaṃ sāṃkhyāḥ paramarṣiṃ prajāpatim sa manye tena rūpeṇa vismāpayati hi svayam
english: Whom the followers of Sāṃkhya call Kapila, the supreme seer, Prajāpati—he, I think, in that very form amazes them by his own self.

sanskrit: āsureḥ prathamaṃ śiṣyaṃ yam āhuś cirajīvinam pañcasrotasi yaḥ satram āste varṣasahasrikam
english: Whom they call Āsuri, the first disciple, the long-lived one, who at the Five-Streams kept a sacrificial session lasting a thousand years—

sanskrit: taṃ samāsīnam āgamya maṇḍalaṃ kāpilaṃ mahat puruṣāvastham avyaktaṃ paramārthaṃ nibodhayat
english: approaching him as he sat within the great circle of Kapila's teaching, Kapila made known to him the supreme truth: the Unmanifest abiding as the Spirit.

sanskrit: iṣṭisatreṇa saṃsiddho bhūyaś ca tapasā muniḥ kṣetrakṣetrajñayor vyaktiṃ bubudhe devadarśanaḥ
english: Perfected by his sacrificial session and further by austerity, that sage, beholder of the gods, came to comprehend the distinction between the Field and the Knower of the Field.

sanskrit: yat tad ekākṣaraṃ brahma nānārūpaṃ pradṛśyate āsurir maṇḍale tasmin pratipede tad avyayam
english: That single imperishable Brahman which appears in manifold forms—that unfailing reality Āsuri attained within that circle of teaching.

sanskrit: tasya pañcaśikhaḥ śiṣyo mānuṣyā payasā bhṛtaḥ brāhmaṇī kapilā nāma kā cid āsīt kuṭumbinī
english: His disciple was Pañcaśikha, nourished by the milk of a human woman; there was a certain brāhmaṇa matron named Kapilā, a householder's wife.

sanskrit: tasyāḥ putratvam āgamya striyāḥ sa pibati stanau tataḥ sa kāpileyatvaṃ lebhe buddhiṃ ca naiṣṭhikīm
english: Coming to be as a son to that woman, he drank at her breasts; thereby he gained the name Kāpileya and an unwavering, perfected understanding.

sanskrit: etan me bhagavān āha kāpileyāya saṃbhavam tasya tat kāpileyatvaṃ sarvavittvam anuttamam
english: This origin of the name Kāpileya the blessed one told to me; that title 'Kāpileya' of his meant an unsurpassed omniscience.

sanskrit: sāmānyaṃ kapilo jñātvā dharmajñānām anuttamam upetya śatam ācāryān mohayām āsa hetubhiḥ
english: Kapila, knowing the common ground, supreme among the knowers of the law, approached the hundred teachers and confounded them with his arguments.

sanskrit: janakas tv abhisaṃraktaḥ kāpileyānudarśanāt utsṛjya śatam ācāryān pṛṣṭhato 'nujagāma tam
english: And Janaka, won over by his beholding of Kāpileya, forsook the hundred teachers and followed close behind him.

sanskrit: tasmai paramakalpāya praṇatāya ca dharmataḥ abravīt paramaṃ mokṣaṃ yat tat sāṃkhyaṃ vidhīyate
english: To him, supremely fit and bowed low according to the law, Kapila declared the supreme liberation, that which is ordained as the Sāṃkhya teaching.

sanskrit: jātinirvedam uktvā hi karmanirvedam abravīt karmanirvedam uktvā ca sarvanirvedam abravīt
english: Having spoken of disillusion with birth, he spoke of disillusion with action; and having spoken of disillusion with action, he spoke of disillusion with all things.

sanskrit: yadarthaṃ karmasaṃsargaḥ karmaṇāṃ ca phalodayaḥ tad anāśvāsikaṃ moghaṃ vināśi calam adhruvam
english: That for the sake of which there is engagement in action, and the rising of action's fruits—that is unreliable, empty, perishable, unstable, impermanent.

sanskrit: dṛśyamāne vināśe ca pratyakṣe lokasākṣike āgamāt param astīti bruvann api parājitaḥ
english: With destruction seen plainly before the eyes, witnessed by all the world, even he who says 'beyond this, on scriptural authority, something exists' stands defeated.

sanskrit: anātmā hy ātmano mṛtyuḥ kleśo mṛtyur jarāmayaḥ ātmānaṃ manyate mohāt tad asamyak paraṃ matam
english: For the non-self is the death of the self—affliction is death, and so are old age and disease; out of delusion one takes this for the Self, and that is held to be the foremost error.

sanskrit: atha ced evam apy asti yal loke nopapadyate ajaro 'yam amṛtyuś ca rājāsau manyate tathā
english: But suppose there be such a thing as does not arise within the world—'this one is ageless and deathless'—and the king too thinks so:

sanskrit: asti nāstīti cāpy etat tasminn asati lakṣaṇe kim adhiṣṭhāya tad brūyāl lokayātrāviniścayam
english: yet this very 'it is' and 'it is not'—when no mark of it can be found, upon what could one rest in declaring the settled course of worldly life?

sanskrit: pratyakṣaṃ hy etayor mūlaṃ kṛtāntaitihyayor api pratyakṣo hy āgamo 'bhinnaḥ kṛtānto vā na kiṃ cana
english: For direct perception is the root of both—of doctrine and of tradition alike; perception is one with scripture, undivided, and apart from it doctrine is nothing at all.

sanskrit: yatra tatrānumāne 'sti kṛtaṃ bhāvayate 'pi vā anyo jīvaḥ śarīrasya nāstikānāṃ mate smṛtaḥ
english: Wherever there is inference, whether one posits a thing as done or imagines it so, a living principle distinct from the body is, in the view of the deniers, held to be remembered.

sanskrit: reto vaṭakaṇīkāyāṃ ghṛtapākādhivāsanam jātismṛtir ayaskāntaḥ sūryakānto 'mbubhakṣaṇam
english: The seed within the banyan's tiny grain, the lingering fragrance from the cooking of ghee, the memory of past births, the loadstone, the sunstone, the drinking of water—

sanskrit: pretya bhūtātyayaś caiva devatābhyupayācanam mṛte karmanivṛttiś ca pramāṇam iti niścayaḥ
english: the passing of beings after death, the supplication of deities, and the ceasing of action when one is dead—these, it is concluded, are the proofs.

sanskrit: na tv ete hetavaḥ santi ye ke cin mūrtisaṃsthitāḥ amartyasya hi martyena sāmānyaṃ nopapadyate
english: But these grounds, whatever they be, hold only for things fixed in bodily form; for the immortal can have nothing in common with the mortal.

sanskrit: avidyākarmaceṣṭānāṃ ke cid āhuḥ punarbhavam kāraṇaṃ lobhamohau tu doṣāṇāṃ ca niṣevaṇam
english: Some declare that for ignorance, action, and striving there is rebirth; and that the cause is greed and delusion, and the indulgence of faults.

sanskrit: avidyāṃ kṣetram āhur hi karma bījaṃ tathā kṛtam tṛṣṇāsaṃjananaṃ sneha eṣa teṣāṃ punarbhavaḥ
english: For they call ignorance the field, and action thus performed the seed; attachment is what engenders craving—such, for them, is rebirth.

sanskrit: tasmin vyūḍhe ca dagdhe ca citte maraṇadharmiṇi anyo 'nyāj jāyate dehas tam āhuḥ sattvasaṃkṣayam
english: When that mind, subject to death, has been dispersed and burnt away, another body is born from another; this they call the dissolution of the being.

sanskrit: yadā sa rūpataś cānyo jātitaḥ śrutito 'rthataḥ katham asmin sa ity eva saṃbandhaḥ syād asaṃhitaḥ
english: When the new one is other in form, in birth, in learning, and in substance, how could there be the relation 'this is the same as that,' when there is no real connection?

sanskrit: evaṃ sati ca kā prītir dānavidyātapobalaiḥ yad anyācaritaṃ karma sarvam anyaḥ prapadyate
english: And this being so, what joy is there in the powers of gift-giving, learning, and austerity, when all the action performed by one is reaped by another?

sanskrit: yadā hy ayam ihaivānyaiḥ prākṛtair duḥkhito bhavet sukhitair duḥkhitair vāpi dṛśyo 'py asya vinirṇayaḥ
english: For when this one here is made to suffer by other natural beings, whether they be happy or themselves in pain, the verdict upon him is plain to see.
